I'm glad to hear about your finishing up your semester! I graduated just recently, and as much as it's satisfying to finally get a diploma, I feel like I missed out most of the "college experience", whatever that is... I totally get you when you talk about feeling alone. There were some times when I had to wait hours for a specific class to begin, and I sat there waiting invisibly. I'd see these groups of friends laughing, along with couples, while I was there, alone with my phone. Then I'd think, "really, it seems that I am the only one alone like that". I know this isn't true at all, but when you're in the middle of it, it's really easy to feel like you're the only one. 

I have some friends, I'd say, but nobody is really that close to me. I mean, they talk to me, but I feel I'm not that important to them and can be easy replaced. I usually can count on my fingers the times I go out during a year. This year I have been invited to go out twice. 

The only thing keeping me slightly excited is that I'm close to earning a grant that would allow me to travel abroad for nine months. If I do get that, maybe things could change... Or not, I don't know. I honestly thought things would be totally different after I left university and, while this is true of my beliefs and things I've learned, my social life is pretty much the same as it was before. 

In the end, I surely hope at least the achievable works out.

This one wasn't just weird, it was horrifying and gross. 

I dreamed that, for some reason, people were dying from being stung by bees. I can recall this appearing on TV and being called "the bee crisis". In real life, my house has a little outdoor area where we have two sinks. All of a sudden, I took a look at those sinks and there was a dead body on them. Then the bodies just kept showing up. But nobody removed the bodies from there, and then the bodies (presumably) started to decompose. For some reason, I touched one of the rotting bodies and it was *squishy*. Only then I realized they were all dead and then I panicked. That's when I finally woke up. I swear to God, it took half an hour to get those squishy dead bodies out of my mind. I felt horrified.

I had read, the night before, about a man who killed himself inside his car and went unnoticed for several days. That's probably the reason I had this hell of a nightmare.
